name: Real-Time Presence, Heartbeat Hysteresis & Hybrid Fan-Out
tagline: Never broadcast every user's presence heartbeat globally—use lazy pull/subscription for presence and switch from write-push to read-pull above ~500 channel members.
purpose: Real-time presence uses periodic WebSocket heartbeats into TTL-backed Redis keys (`SETEX 45s`) with online/offline hysteresis, paired with hybrid push/pull fan-out for small vs. massive channels.

spark.summary: Real-time presence uses periodic WebSocket heartbeats into TTL-backed Redis keys (`SETEX 45s`) with online/offline hysteresis, paired with hybrid push/pull fan-out for small vs. massive channels.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, heartbeat Hysteresis & Hybrid Fan-Out, never broadcast every user's presence heartbeat globally—use lazy pull/subscription for presence and switch from write-push to read-pull above ~500 channel members.
spark.byteSummary:
Broadcasting online/offline status changes for 50M concurrent users to every contact on every flaky mobile reconnect triggers a quadratic fan-out storm (`O(N * F)` events/sec).

Production presence systems decouple **Heartbeat Ingestion** (clients ping every 30s, refreshing `SETEX presence:user_id 45s` in Redis) from **Lazy Presence Subscriptions** (clients only subscribe to visible friends/active DM headers) and apply **Offline Hysteresis** (wait 45s+ before flipping offline so brief tunnel drops don't flicker).

For message delivery, small groups/DMs (<= 500 members) push directly via Redis Pub/Sub to sticky WebSocket gateways, while 100K-member Discord guilds switch to **Hybrid/Pull** or sharded guild relays.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Real-Time Presence, Heartbeat Hysteresis & Hybrid Fan-Out without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, heartbeat Hysteresis & Hybrid Fan-Out, never broadcast every user's presence heartbeat globally—use lazy pull/subscription for presence and switch from write-push to read-pull above ~500 channel members.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.

options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

sectionDiagram.title: Durability, Consistency & Recovery

cards.label: Gap Sync on Reconnect
cards.detail: Clients pass last_seen_seq on WebSocket resume to fetch any missed messages during brief drops.

cards.label: Monotonic Read Cursor
cards.detail: Store max(read_seq) per (user, channel) so an old mobile device never rewinds desktop read state.

cards.label: Client-Generated UUID
cards.detail: Deduplicate retries by client_msg_id so poor cellular connections never double-post.
